_about: YouGov polls commissioned by The Australia Institute that do NOT channel into the auspol-tracker data model (no voting intention is published - the reports' own methodology statements record 'Is voting intention published? No'). Compiled by reading the Institute's published full-report PDFs; filed 2026-11-01 with the October 2026 'Friends and threats to Australia' brief; the October 2025 'Poll on US' brief (eleven questions on Trump, the alliance and AUKUS, n=1,500) was added 2026-11-02. YouGov's own fortnightly News24 series is a separate house (news24-one-offs.json).
_readme: Verification: every figure was read from the published report PDF (Polling - Friends and threats to Australia, October 2026; cdn.australiainstitute.org.au .../Polling-Friends-and-threats-to-Australia-Web.pdf). The main table transposes the report's summary Table 1 (fact-checked column-wise against the country narratives, which put the United States first) so its rows read the answer options; rows reconcile to 100 within 0dp rounding, and every country column likewise sums to its summary-table row. The United States cuts are the report's appendix Tables 3, 4 and 5 verbatim (its gender and age columns are filed as separate by-gender / by-age tables per store convention); the report's ALP/COA/GRE/ON/IND/UND abbreviations are expanded to the site's group names. Each country beyond the United States also has gender/age/state/vote crosstabs in appendix Tables 2 and 6-16; those are not filed, so the one entry's cut tables stay the United States' own. Fieldwork 6-12 October 2026, n=1,100, online panel, Australian Polling Council compliant. Verification (October 2025 brief added 2026-11-02): every figure was read by a scripted parse of the report PDF (Aus-Institute-Poll-on-US-Oct25-summary-30102025.pdf) and reconciled - every option-row column sums to 100 within 0dp rounding in both of the report's banners, and wrapped labels were re-joined before filing. Each question files its Total summary plus By gender and By age (the report's banner AI 1) and By state and By voting intention (banner AI 2); the report's ALP/COA/GRE/ON/IND/UND abbreviations are expanded to the site's group names, and NET rows are kept verbatim as printed. US5 asked about Australia, the United States and the world - its summary table carries all three; group cuts are filed for the Australia answer only. Fieldwork 23-30 October 2025, n=1,500 (effective 1,050), online panel; the poll published no voting intention (its APC long disclosure statement records 'Is voting intention published? No'), so nothing of it lands in the tracker's poll tables: cdn.australiainstitute.org.au .../AI_October_US_Poll_Polling_Council_Methodology_Statement_Oct25.pdf.

entries.question: Do you feel more or less secure in Australia since the election of Donald Trump as President of the United States?
entries.notes: Half (48%) feel less secure in Australia since Donald Trump's election as US President; only 13% feel more secure. Greens voters are the most uneasy (72% less secure); One Nation's divide between no change (41%) and more secure (28%). Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Do you think the United States is a reliable or unreliable security ally for Australia?
entries.notes: Australians split on the United States as a security ally - 44% reliable against 47% unreliable. Coalition (62% reliable) and One Nation (64%) voters are comfortable; Greens (18%) and Labor (39%) voters are not. Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: If Australia was threatened, how confident are you that United States President Donald Trump would defend Australia and Australia's interests?
entries.notes: 51% are confident President Trump would defend Australia and Australia's interests if it was threatened; 40% are not at all confident. Coalition (65%) and One Nation (71%) voters are confident, Greens (29%) deeply not. Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Do you think Australia's interests are served better by:
entries.notes: 46% say Australia's interests are served better by a more independent foreign policy; 32% say a closer alliance with the United States. Coalition voters break the other way (51% alliance, 28% independent). Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Do you think Donald Trump being elected as President of the United States is a good or bad thing for Australia, the United States and the world?
entries.notes: Asked for Australia, the United States and the world separately (the summary table's three columns; group cuts are filed for the Australia answer). Half (50%) call Trump's election bad for Australia - and 54% say bad for the United States itself, 56% for the world. One Nation voters are the lone enthusiasts (47% good, for Australia). Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Do you believe the United States has become more or less democratic under President Donald Trump?
entries.notes: Half (50%) believe the United States has become less democratic under President Trump; 15% say more. Greens (69%) and Labor (59%) voters lead the less-democratic read; One Nation (28%) leads the more. Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: How safe or unsafe would you feel travelling to the United States?
entries.notes: 51% would feel unsafe travelling to the United States, against 40% who would feel safe. Men (48%) feel safer about the trip than women (33%). Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said Australia and the United States “share values” of “democracy and the rule of law”. Do you agree or disagree that Australia “shares values” with the United States under President Trump?
entries.notes: Asked whether Australia “shares values” with the United States under President Trump (Defence Minister Marles had said the two share values of “democracy and the rule of law”), only 32% agree; 49% disagree. Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: AUKUS is a $368 billion agreement between Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom under which Australia is supposed to acquire nuclear-powered submarines. Do you think pursuing the AUKUS security agreement is in Australia’s best interests?
entries.notes: 41% think pursuing the AUKUS security agreement is in Australia's best interests, 26% think it is not, and a third (33%) are unsure. Coalition (56%) and One Nation (50%) voters are sold; 54% of Greens say no. Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Do you think the AUKUS security agreement between Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom makes Australia more safe or less safe?
entries.notes: 46% think the AUKUS security agreement makes Australia more safe, 17% less safe; 37% are unsure. Men (57%) are much surer it helps than women (36%). Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: Would you support or oppose an Australian parliamentary inquiry into the AUKUS security agreement?
entries.notes: 53% would support an Australian parliamentary inquiry into the AUKUS security agreement; 16% would oppose. Support is highest among Greens (76%) and Labor (61%) voters. Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd).

entries.question: A friendly country is one you view as safe and trustworthy. A threatening country is one you view with caution or suspicion. For each country below, do you view them as a friend or a threat to Australia?
entries.notes: The five countries were presented in a random order. Only 16% see the United States as a close friend (50% a friend or close friend against 42% a threat or major threat); New Zealand is a friend or close friend to 97% (77% close), Indonesia to 64%, China to 24% and Russia to 7%. By voting intention, One Nation voters are warmest on the US (36% close friend, 69% friend or close friend, 23% threat) and Greens voters the coldest (1% close friend, 70% threat). Commissioned by The Australia Institute; fieldwork and weighting by YouGov (YouGov Galaxy Pty Ltd), APC methodology statement linked from the report.
